evidenceSections.sourceIdentity: JCGM 200:2012, International Vocabulary of Metrology (VIM), 3rd edition
evidenceSections.supports: That calibration is a two-step operation: first establishing a relation between quantity values with measurement uncertainties provided by standards and the corresponding indications with their uncertainties, then using that relation to obtain a measurement result from an indication.

limitations: This is measurement calibration of an instrument against a standard. It does not define calibration of a probabilistic forecast, which is a different concept sharing the word. A page on forecast calibration must not cite this definition, and this source establishes nothing about model confidence.
